pendingCompletion.completionSummary: Outcome: Cylinder (shaft) bonds now render on the modern and legacy tiers. Changed: replaced the Cylinder's `glNewList` display-list path (broken via glGenLists rejection on Core + VBO read-after-freeBuffers use-after-free) with immediate-mode emission (GL_QUAD_STRIP / GL_LINES) over the kept-alive vertex/normal buffers; added a const `drawImmediate()` helper and had draw()/drawMulti() cast away const for the one-time lazy initialize(); stripped the debug qDebug lines from glwidget.cpp. Evidence: commit 5ffdaeb6b on fix-modern-tier-pick-and-axes, pushed to thosoo/avogadro; build clean; ctest 34/34 pass under xvfb. Tests: `cmake --build build` clean; `ctest --test-dir build` 34/34 green under xvfb-run (parity/compatibility/pick suites need a real X display). Unresolved: GitHub Actions Qt6 CI not yet confirmed green on the pushed commit. Next: watch the CI run on the branch.
pendingCompletion.verificationSummary:
Behavioral: cylinder bonds render on modern/legacy tiers (user-confirmed working). Build: cmake --build build --parallel --target avogadro → 100% Built target avogadro, no errors. Tests: ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure under xvfb-run 1280x1024x24 → 34/34 passed (paritybsdy, paritysphere, paritystick, paritywire, compatibility, glselectoverflow, meshstream, threadedparity, renderbench, visualparity, hidpiviewport all pass with a real X display; offscreen-only runs abort on those same suites). Note: CI (GitHub Actions) has not been run/confirmed on the pushed commit yet.
Executor-asserted outcome claims (independent review required):
[{"required":"executed","kind":"behavioral-check","evidence":"Committed 5ffdaeb6b on branch fix-modern-tier-pick-and-axes (pushed to github.com/thosoo/avogadro); user confirmed 'it works' — cylinder shafts render. Build clean; ctest 34/34 pass under xvfb-run."}]

findingGroups.title: Cylinder rendering fix
findings: Shafts now render — replaced broken glNewList display-list capture (glGenLists rejected on Core + VBO read-after-freeBuffers use-after-free) with immediate-mode GL_QUAD_STRIP/GL_LINES over the kept-alive vertex/normal buffers.
Fixed a const-discarding compile error (cylinder_p.cpp:197/225) by adding a const drawImmediate() helper and casting away const for the one-time lazy initialize() in draw()/drawMulti().
Removed the [ctx]/[render START] debug qDebug lines left in glwidget.cpp during investigation; the fixed-function lighting restoration was already committed separately.

findingGroups.title: Verification
findings: avogadro plugin builds clean (cmake --build build --parallel --target avogadro → 100% Built target avogadro).
ctest 34/34 pass under xvfb-run; the parity/compatibility/pick suites require a real X display and abort under offscreen-only runs.

Harness caveat: a standalone QOffscreenSurface/FBO test read stale framebuffer data and wouldn't render raw immediate-mode triangles there, but the display-list path rendered in that same context and the cone already uses immediate mode in GLWidget, so that was a test-context artifact, not a fix defect.

findingGroups.title: Cylinder rendering fix
findings: Shafts now render — replaced broken glNewList display-list capture (glGenLists rejected on Core + VBO read-after-freeBuffers use-after-free) with immediate-mode GL_QUAD_STRIP/GL_LINES over the kept-alive vertex/normal buffers.
Fixed a const-discarding compile error (cylinder_p.cpp:197/225) by adding a const drawImmediate() helper and casting away const for the one-time lazy initialize() in draw()/drawMulti().
Removed the [ctx]/[render START] debug qDebug lines left in glwidget.cpp during investigation; the fixed-function lighting restoration was already committed separately.

findingGroups.title: Verification
findings: avogadro plugin builds clean (cmake --build build --parallel --target avogadro → 100% Built target avogadro).
ctest 34/34 pass under xvfb-run; the parity/compatibility/pick suites require a real X display and abort under offscreen-only runs.

Harness caveat: a standalone QOffscreenSurface/FBO test read stale framebuffer data and wouldn't render raw immediate-mode triangles there, but the display-list path rendered in that same context and the cone already uses immediate mode in GLWidget, so that was a test-context artifact, not a fix defect.

findingGroups.title: Cylinder rendering fix
findings: Shafts now render — replaced broken glNewList display-list capture (glGenLists rejected on Core + VBO read-after-freeBuffers use-after-free) with immediate-mode GL_QUAD_STRIP/GL_LINES over the kept-alive vertex/normal buffers.
Fixed a const-discarding compile error (cylinder_p.cpp:197/225) by adding a const drawImmediate() helper and casting away const for the one-time lazy initialize() in draw()/drawMulti().
Removed the [ctx]/[render START] debug qDebug lines left in glwidget.cpp during investigation; the fixed-function lighting restoration was already committed separately.

findingGroups.title: Verification
findings: avogadro plugin builds clean (cmake --build build --parallel --target avogadro → 100% Built target avogadro).
ctest 34/34 pass under xvfb-run; the parity/compatibility/pick suites require a real X display and abort under offscreen-only runs.

Harness caveat: a standalone QOffscreenSurface/FBO test read stale framebuffer data and wouldn't render raw immediate-mode triangles there, but the display-list path rendered in that same context and the cone already uses immediate mode in GLWidget, so that was a test-context artifact, not a fix defect.

findingGroups.title: Cylinder rendering fix
findings: Shafts now render — replaced broken glNewList display-list capture (glGenLists rejected on Core + VBO read-after-freeBuffers use-after-free) with immediate-mode GL_QUAD_STRIP/GL_LINES over the kept-alive vertex/normal buffers.
Fixed a const-discarding compile error (cylinder_p.cpp:197/225) by adding a const drawImmediate() helper and casting away const for the one-time lazy initialize() in draw()/drawMulti().
Removed the [ctx]/[render START] debug qDebug lines left in glwidget.cpp during investigation; the fixed-function lighting restoration was already committed separately.

findingGroups.title: Verification
findings: avogadro plugin builds clean (cmake --build build --parallel --target avogadro → 100% Built target avogadro).
ctest 34/34 pass under xvfb-run; the parity/compatibility/pick suites require a real X display and abort under offscreen-only runs.

Harness caveat: a standalone QOffscreenSurface/FBO test read stale framebuffer data and wouldn't render raw immediate-mode triangles there, but the display-list path rendered in that same context and the cone already uses immediate mode in GLWidget, so that was a test-context artifact, not a fix defect.

findingGroups.title: Cylinder rendering fix
findings: Shafts now render — replaced broken glNewList display-list capture (glGenLists rejected on Core + VBO read-after-freeBuffers use-after-free) with immediate-mode GL_QUAD_STRIP/GL_LINES over the kept-alive vertex/normal buffers.
Fixed a const-discarding compile error (cylinder_p.cpp:197/225) by adding a const drawImmediate() helper and casting away const for the one-time lazy initialize() in draw()/drawMulti().
Removed the [ctx]/[render START] debug qDebug lines left in glwidget.cpp during investigation; the fixed-function lighting restoration was already committed separately.

findingGroups.title: Verification
findings: avogadro plugin builds clean (cmake --build build --parallel --target avogadro → 100% Built target avogadro).
ctest 34/34 pass under xvfb-run; the parity/compatibility/pick suites require a real X display and abort under offscreen-only runs.

Harness caveat: a standalone QOffscreenSurface/FBO test read stale framebuffer data and wouldn't render raw immediate-mode triangles there, but the display-list path rendered in that same context and the cone already uses immediate mode in GLWidget, so that was a test-context artifact, not a fix defect.

findingGroups.title: Cylinder rendering fix
findings: Shafts now render — replaced broken glNewList display-list capture (glGenLists rejected on Core + VBO read-after-freeBuffers use-after-free) with immediate-mode GL_QUAD_STRIP/GL_LINES over the kept-alive vertex/normal buffers.
Fixed a const-discarding compile error (cylinder_p.cpp:197/225) by adding a const drawImmediate() helper and casting away const for the one-time lazy initialize() in draw()/drawMulti().
Removed the [ctx]/[render START] debug qDebug lines left in glwidget.cpp during investigation; the fixed-function lighting restoration was already committed separately.

findingGroups.title: Verification
findings: avogadro plugin builds clean (cmake --build build --parallel --target avogadro → 100% Built target avogadro).
ctest 34/34 pass under xvfb-run; the parity/compatibility/pick suites require a real X display and abort under offscreen-only runs.

Harness caveat: a standalone QOffscreenSurface/FBO test read stale framebuffer data and wouldn't render raw immediate-mode triangles there, but the display-list path rendered in that same context and the cone already uses immediate mode in GLWidget, so that was a test-context artifact, not a fix defect.

findingGroups.title: Cylinder rendering fix
findings: Shafts now render — replaced broken glNewList display-list capture (glGenLists rejected on Core + VBO read-after-freeBuffers use-after-free) with immediate-mode GL_QUAD_STRIP/GL_LINES over the kept-alive vertex/normal buffers.
Fixed a const-discarding compile error (cylinder_p.cpp:197/225) by adding a const drawImmediate() helper and casting away const for the one-time lazy initialize() in draw()/drawMulti().
Removed the [ctx]/[render START] debug qDebug lines left in glwidget.cpp during investigation; the fixed-function lighting restoration was already committed separately.

findingGroups.title: Verification
findings: avogadro plugin builds clean (cmake --build build --parallel --target avogadro → 100% Built target avogadro).
ctest 34/34 pass under xvfb-run; the parity/compatibility/pick suites require a real X display and abort under offscreen-only runs.

Harness caveat: a standalone QOffscreenSurface/FBO test read stale framebuffer data and wouldn't render raw immediate-mode triangles there, but the display-list path rendered in that same context and the cone already uses immediate mode in GLWidget, so that was a test-context artifact, not a fix defect.

# Completion Audit — fix-modern-tier-pick-and-axes

## Verdict summary

The **implementation** is real and verified: I independently built (`100%`), ran the full suite under xvfb (**34/34 passed**), confirmed both GitHub workflows **success on the exact HEAD SHA 5ffdaeb6b** (superseding the summary's stale "unresolved CI" note), confirmed all spec scenarios have code+test evidence, and inspected fresh PNGs natively (bond shafts render on modern tier, visually identical to legacy). HEAD is pushed (origin == HEAD).

The **OpenSpec artifact layer** is what fails: the change's central defect (missing axes cylinder) was finally fixed by *replacing* the display-list path with immediate mode (commit 5ffdaeb6b), but the authoritative artifacts still document the old mechanism as the verified fix — `design.md` D4 ("Cylinder::initialize() compiles display lists defensively", leak table row "cylinder | display list … | **no**") and the `tasks.md` 3.2 note ("The display list now captures the client addresses … so the axes cylinder shafts render on the modern tier") both describe code that no longer exists at HEAD. Additionally, the design/proposal/spec deltas (incl. the D7 lighting design) are **uncommitted** in the working tree. Contract items 3 and 6 are contradicted; item 7 is weakened.

## Required fixes

1. [MED] Update `design.md` (D4 section + leak-analysis table) and the `tasks.md` 3.2 verification note to record the actual final fix — display list replaced by immediate-mode `drawImmediate()` with retained buffers, per commit 5ffdaeb6b's rationale — so the authoritative OpenSpec artifacts match HEAD's `cylinder_p.cpp`.
2. [MED] Commit the uncommitted OpenSpec artifact deltas (`design.md`, `proposal.md`, `specs/gpu-rendering-pipeline/spec.md`) so the repository is coherent for subsequent OpenSpec verification/archive work.

# Completion Audit — fix-modern-tier-pick-and-axes

## Verdict summary

The **implementation** is real and verified: I independently built (`100%`), ran the full suite under xvfb (**34/34 passed**), confirmed both GitHub workflows **success on the exact HEAD SHA 5ffdaeb6b** (superseding the summary's stale "unresolved CI" note), confirmed all spec scenarios have code+test evidence, and inspected fresh PNGs natively (bond shafts render on modern tier, visually identical to legacy). HEAD is pushed (origin == HEAD).

The **OpenSpec artifact layer** is what fails: the change's central defect (missing axes cylinder) was finally fixed by *replacing* the display-list path with immediate mode (commit 5ffdaeb6b), but the authoritative artifacts still document the old mechanism as the verified fix — `design.md` D4 ("Cylinder::initialize() compiles display lists defensively", leak table row "cylinder | display list … | **no**") and the `tasks.md` 3.2 note ("The display list now captures the client addresses … so the axes cylinder shafts render on the modern tier") both describe code that no longer exists at HEAD. Additionally, the design/proposal/spec deltas (incl. the D7 lighting design) are **uncommitted** in the working tree. Contract items 3 and 6 are contradicted; item 7 is weakened.

1. [MED] Update `design.md` (D4 section + leak-analysis table) and the `tasks.md` 3.2 verification note to record the actual final fix — display list replaced by immediate-mode `drawImmediate()` with retained buffers, per commit 5ffdaeb6b's rationale — so the authoritative OpenSpec artifacts match HEAD's `cylinder_p.cpp`.

# Completion Audit — fix-modern-tier-pick-and-axes

## Verdict summary

The **implementation** is real and verified: I independently built (`100%`), ran the full suite under xvfb (**34/34 passed**), confirmed both GitHub workflows **success on the exact HEAD SHA 5ffdaeb6b** (superseding the summary's stale "unresolved CI" note), confirmed all spec scenarios have code+test evidence, and inspected fresh PNGs natively (bond shafts render on modern tier, visually identical to legacy). HEAD is pushed (origin == HEAD).

The **OpenSpec artifact layer** is what fails: the change's central defect (missing axes cylinder) was finally fixed by *replacing* the display-list path with immediate mode (commit 5ffdaeb6b), but the authoritative artifacts still document the old mechanism as the verified fix — `design.md` D4 ("Cylinder::initialize() compiles display lists defensively", leak table row "cylinder | display list … | **no**") and the `tasks.md` 3.2 note ("The display list now captures the client addresses … so the axes cylinder shafts render on the modern tier") both describe code that no longer exists at HEAD. Additionally, the design/proposal/spec deltas (incl. the D7 lighting design) are **uncommitted** in the working tree. Contract items 3 and 6 are contradicted; item 7 is weakened.

## Required fixes

1. [MED] Update `design.md` (D4 section + leak-analysis table) and the `tasks.md` 3.2 verification note to record the actual final fix — display list replaced by immediate-mode `drawImmediate()` with retained buffers, per commit 5ffdaeb6b's rationale — so the authoritative OpenSpec artifacts match HEAD's `cylinder_p.cpp`.
2. [MED] Commit the uncommitted OpenSpec artifact deltas (`design.md`, `proposal.md`, `specs/gpu-rendering-pipeline/spec.md`) so the repository is coherent for subsequent OpenSpec verification/archive work.

Advisory (non-blocking): [LOW] `#include <QDebug>` added to `cylinder_p.cpp` by 5ffdaeb6b is now unused; pre-existing `snapshottessellator::emitTransparentBonds` bondIndex desync remains explicitly out of scope (reviewer-noted).

The **implementation** is real and verified: I independently built (`100%`), ran the full suite under xvfb (**34/34 passed**), confirmed both GitHub workflows **success on the exact HEAD SHA 5ffdaeb6b** (superseding the summary's stale "unresolved CI" note), confirmed all spec scenarios have code+test evidence, and inspected fresh PNGs natively (bond shafts render on modern tier, visually identical to legacy). HEAD is pushed (origin == HEAD).

The **OpenSpec artifact layer** is what fails: the change's central defect (missing axes cylinder) was finally fixed by *replacing* the display-list path with immediate mode (commit 5ffdaeb6b), but the authoritative artifacts still document the old mechanism as the verified fix — `design.md` D4 ("Cylinder::initialize() compiles display lists defensively", leak table row "cylinder | display list … | **no**") and the `tasks.md` 3.2 note ("The display list now captures the client addresses … so the axes cylinder shafts render on the modern tier") both describe code that no longer exists at HEAD. Additionally, the design/proposal/spec deltas (incl. the D7 lighting design) are **uncommitted** in the working tree. Contract items 3 and 6 are contradicted; item 7 is weakened.

## Required fixes

1. [MED] Update `design.md` (D4 section + leak-analysis table) and the `tasks.md` 3.2 verification note to record the actual final fix — display list replaced by immediate-mode `drawImmediate()` with retained buffers, per commit 5ffdaeb6b's rationale — so the authoritative OpenSpec artifacts match HEAD's `cylinder_p.cpp`.
2. [MED] Commit the uncommitted OpenSpec artifact deltas (`design.md`, `proposal.md`, `specs/gpu-rendering-pipeline/spec.md`) so the repository is coherent for subsequent OpenSpec verification/archive work.

Advisory (non-blocking): [LOW] `#include <QDebug>` added to `cylinder_p.cpp` by 5ffdaeb6b is now unused; pre-existing `snapshottessellator::emitTransparentBonds` bondIndex desync remains explicitly out of scope (reviewer-noted).

# Completion Audit — fix-modern-tier-pick-and-axes

## Verdict summary

The **implementation** is real and verified: I independently built (`100%`), ran the full suite under xvfb (**34/34 passed**), confirmed both GitHub workflows **success on the exact HEAD SHA 5ffdaeb6b** (superseding the summary's stale "unresolved CI" note), confirmed all spec scenarios have code+test evidence, and inspected fresh PNGs natively (bond shafts render on modern tier, visually identical to legacy). HEAD is pushed (origin == HEAD).

The **OpenSpec artifact layer** is what fails: the change's central defect (missing axes cylinder) was finally fixed by *replacing* the display-list path with immediate mode (commit 5ffdaeb6b), but the authoritative artifacts still document the old mechanism as the verified fix — `design.md` D4 ("Cylinder::initialize() compiles display lists defensively", leak table row "cylinder | display list … | **no**") and the `tasks.md` 3.2 note ("The display list now captures the client addresses … so the axes cylinder shafts render on the modern tier") both describe code that no longer exists at HEAD. [MED] Update `design.md` (D4 section + leak-analysis table) and the `tasks.md` 3.2 verification note to record the actual final fix — display list replaced by immediate-mode `drawImmediate()` with retained buffers, per commit 5ffdaeb6b's rationale — so the authoritative OpenSpec artifacts match HEAD's `cylinder_p.cpp`.

completionRecap.summary: Outcome: Cylinder (shaft) bonds now render on the modern and legacy tiers. Changed: replaced the Cylinder's `glNewList` display-list path (broken via glGenLists rejection on Core + VBO read-after-freeBuffers use-after-free) with immediate-mode emission (GL_QUAD_STRIP / GL_LINES) over the kept-alive vertex/normal buffers; added a const `drawImmediate()` helper and had draw()/drawMulti() cast away const for the one-time lazy initialize(); stripped the debug qDebug lines from glwidget.cpp. Evidence: commit 5ffdaeb6b on fix-modern-tier-pick-and-axes, pushed to thosoo/avogadro; build clean; ctest 34/34 pass under xvfb. Tests: `cmake --build build` clean; `ctest --test-dir build` 34/34 green under xvfb-run (parity/compatibility/pick suites need a real X display). Unresolved: GitHub Actions Qt6 CI not yet confirmed green on the pushed commit. Next: watch the CI run on the branch.

goal.completionSummary: Outcome: The "fix-modern-tier-pick-and-axes" OpenSpec change is now verified-complete and coherent. This turn addressed the auditor's disapproval: the change's central fix (immediate-mode cylinder shafts) was implemented and committed, but the authoritative OpenSpec artifacts still documented the old display-list mechanism, and the artifact deltas were uncommitted. Changed: reconciled design.md (leak-table cylinder row, defect-B diagnosis, D4), proposal.md (cylinder bullet), and tasks.md (3.2/3.3/5.2) to describe the actual immediate-mode fix (retained vertex/normal buffers + drawImmediate(), GL_QUAD_STRIP/GL_LINES, no display list); committed the pre-existing defect-C spec requirement (axes glyph keeps material colors after a pick); removed an unused #include <QDebug> from cylinder_p.cpp. Evidence: commits 5ffdaeb6b (code) + 8cd3ca333 (artifacts, pushed) on fix-modern-tier-pick-and-axes; openspec state=all_done, 20/20, 0 remaining. Tests: avogadro builds clean; ctest 34/34 green under xvfb-run (compatibility/renderertier/modernpick + all parity/pick suites). Unresolved: GitHub Actions CI (Qt6 CI + Windows Installer) has not been re-run on the artifact-only commit 8cd3ca333 — but it only touches OpenSpec prose plus an unused include, so it cannot affect the build; the code it documents (5ffdaeb6b) already has green CI on HEAD. Next: optionally trigger the CI workflows to confirm green on 8cd3ca333, then archive the change.

completionRecap.summary: Outcome: Restored every consumer the modern render tier silently dropped — tool overlays (AutoOpt energy/HUD halos, bond-centric labels), captured meshes (orbital/ESP surfaces), unit cells, and the quality/fog settings — so the modern tier matches legacy again. Changed: added a shared bracketed `paintOverlaysAfterFrame()` that flushes tool overlays + meshes + unit cells after the instanced frame on renderModern (both branches), renderCompat, drawLastReady(), and the read-lock fallback (retained frames no longer geometry-only); quality now reaches the backend via `setDetailLevel` rebuild with the mapped level persisted across backend creation; fog added as shader uniforms; honest per-tier slider gating on the compat tier (which no-ops both); TextRenderer glyph quads drawn inline so they render cross-context on the shared GLPainter; emitter diagnostics for dropped/coarsened primitives; removed the dead `SceneBuilder::setQuality` declaration. Evidence: commit 0824c8a33 (code + consumerparitytest/energyhudtest/modernrenderertest + OpenSpec change dir); Windows/MSVC CI runs 41097999976 and 41097979535 both success (build-installer tests + installer, incl. offscreen ctest); reviewer report .pi-glla/reviews/20261028164051-bs7k54-*.md; all 5 reviewer findings accepted and fixed; delta archived to main (7bbf7dc23). Tests: `xvfb-run ctest` → 36/36 pass (0 failed); consumerparity, energyhud, modernrenderer, meshstream all green. Unresolved: none — all required work done, delta synced to main, working tree clean. 2. Every explicit requirement and scenario in the active OpenSpec change has corresponding implementation evidence.

3. OpenSpec task completion accurately reflects the actual codebase state; no checkbox is marked complete merely because work was attempted.

4. Relevant builds, tests, and regression checks pass.

5. No known required work, implementation blocker, knowingly failing relevant test, or silently deferred required task remains.

6. A final comparison of the OpenSpec artifacts against the resulting implementation finds no substantive omission.

7. The repository is left in a coherent state suitable for subsequent OpenSpec verification/archive work.

8. Every mirrored GLLA task is complete (the GLLA task list shows no open tasks), so GLLA's pending-task gate does not refuse completion.

Do not declare the GLLA goal complete based only on previous conversation claims or task checkboxes. Verify against current repository and OpenSpec evidence.

At the start of work, after every context compaction, after every resume, and whenever task state is uncertain:

1. Run:
   openspec status --change "fix-surface-visualization-performance" --json

2. Run:
   openspec instructions apply --change "fix-surface-visualization-performance" --json

3. Treat the returned OpenSpec state, instruction, tasks, context, operationGuidance, and contextFiles as authoritative.

4. Read all contextFiles relevant to the remaining work before modifying code.

Resume from the first genuinely incomplete task. Do not redo completed work unnecessarily.

Implement every remaining required task.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.
- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

If the authoritative OpenSpec task set itself changes after attachment, do not silently ignore the difference or invent an independent plan. Reconcile against a fresh OpenSpec apply response before completion.

Run relevant builds, focused tests, integration tests, and regression checks as work progresses. Fix failures caused by this change rather than bypassing them.

Do not weaken, delete, rewrite, reinterpret, or silently defer OpenSpec requirements merely to make implementation easier.

Do not switch to a different OpenSpec change.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.

- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.
- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.

Use the installed OpenSpec apply workflow/skill as the implementation procedure.

At the start of work, after every context compaction, after every resume, and whenever task state is uncertain:

1. Run:
   openspec status --change "fix-surface-visualization-performance" --json

2. Run:
   openspec instructions apply --change "fix-surface-visualization-performance" --json

3. Treat the returned OpenSpec state, instruction, tasks, context, operationGuidance, and contextFiles as authoritative.

4. Read all contextFiles relevant to the remaining work before modifying code.

Resume from the first genuinely incomplete task. Do not redo completed work unnecessarily.

Implement every remaining required task.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.
- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

If the authoritative OpenSpec task set itself changes after attachment, do not silently ignore the difference or invent an independent plan. Reconcile against a fresh OpenSpec apply response before completion.

Run relevant builds, focused tests, integration tests, and regression checks as work progresses. Fix failures caused by this change rather than bypassing them.

Do not weaken, delete, rewrite, reinterpret, or silently defer OpenSpec requirements merely to make implementation easier.

Do not switch to a different OpenSpec change.

If OpenSpec reports state="blocked", resolve the missing required planning artifact through the OpenSpec workflow before continuing implementation. Do not invent missing requirements merely to get past the block.

If OpenSpec reports state="all_done", do not immediately declare success. Perform the final verification below first.

Before claiming completion, independently re-read:

- the current OpenSpec status;
- the current OpenSpec apply instructions;
- all relevant OpenSpec artifacts;
- the repository diff and working-tree state;
- the actual build/test/regression outputs.

2. Every explicit requirement and scenario in the active OpenSpec change has corresponding implementation evidence.

3. OpenSpec task completion accurately reflects the actual codebase state; no checkbox is marked complete merely because work was attempted.

5. No known required work, implementation blocker, knowingly failing relevant test, or silently deferred required task remains.

Do not declare the GLLA goal complete based only on previous conversation claims or task checkboxes. Verify against current repository and OpenSpec evidence.

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.

durableSolution.durableFix: Capture the future from QtConcurrent::map(...): QFuture<void> mapFuture = QtConcurrent::map(shells, processPoint/processDensity); mapFuture.waitForFinished(); — inside the run lambda of both startCubeCalculationAsync and startCubeDensityCalculationAsync. This makes the run worker block until the map truly completes, so the QFutureWatcher's finished signal (and calculationComplete) fires only after all workers are done, eliminating the premature cleanup. - GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".

durableDeferRecommendation.durableFix: Capture the future from QtConcurrent::map(...): QFuture<void> mapFuture = QtConcurrent::map(shells, processPoint/processDensity); mapFuture.waitForFinished(); — inside the run lambda of both startCubeCalculationAsync and startCubeDensityCalculationAsync. This makes the run worker block until the map truly completes, so the QFutureWatcher's finished signal (and calculationComplete) fires only after all workers are done, eliminating the premature cleanup. Removed all debug instrumentation…

durableSolution.durableFix: Capture the future from QtConcurrent::map(...): QFuture<void> mapFuture = QtConcurrent::map(shells, processPoint/processDensity); mapFuture.waitForFinished(); — inside the run lambda of both startCubeCalculationAsync and startCubeDensityCalculationAsync. This makes the run worker block until the map truly completes, so the QFutureWatcher's finished signal (and calculationComplete) fires only after all workers are done, eliminating the premature cleanup. Removed all debug instrumentation (CPP/CUBE/THREAD-CHECK logs, /tmp/cpp_trace.log, unused QDebug/QThread includes in cube.h).

durableDeferRecommendation.durableFix: Capture the future from QtConcurrent::map(...): QFuture<void> mapFuture = QtConcurrent::map(shells, processPoint/processDensity); mapFuture.waitForFinished(); — inside the run lambda of both startCubeCalculationAsync and startCubeDensityCalculationAsync. This makes the run worker block until the map truly completes, so the QFutureWatcher's finished signal (and calculationComplete) fires only after all workers are done, eliminating the premature cleanup. Removed all debug instrumentation…

durableSolution.reason: Root cause of the OpenQube async segfault pinned by instrumented gdb evidence, and fixed at the source.
durableSolution.durableFix: Capture the future from QtConcurrent::map(...): QFuture<void> mapFuture = QtConcurrent::map(shells, processPoint/processDensity); mapFuture.waitForFinished(); — inside the run lambda of both startCubeCalculationAsync and startCubeDensityCalculationAsync. This makes the run worker block until the map truly completes, so the QFutureWatcher's finished signal (and calculationComplete) fires only after all workers are done, eliminating the premature cleanup. Removed all debug instrumentation (CPP/CUBE/THREAD-CHECK logs, /tmp/cpp_trace.log, unused QDebug/QThread includes in cube.h).

At the start of work, after every context compaction, after every resume, and whenever task state is uncertain:

1. Run:
   openspec status --change "fix-surface-visualization-performance" --json

2. Run:
   openspec instructions apply --change "fix-surface-visualization-performance" --json

3. Treat the returned OpenSpec state, instruction, tasks, context, operationGuidance, and contextFiles as authoritative.

4. Read all contextFiles relevant to the remaining work before modifying code.

Resume from the first genuinely incomplete task. Do not redo completed work unnecessarily.

Implement every remaining required task.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.
- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

If the authoritative OpenSpec task set itself changes after attachment, do not silently ignore the difference or invent an independent plan. Reconcile against a fresh OpenSpec apply response before completion.

Run relevant builds, focused tests, integration tests, and regression checks as work progresses. Fix failures caused by this change rather than bypassing them.

Do not weaken, delete, rewrite, reinterpret, or silently defer OpenSpec requirements merely to make implementation easier.

Do not switch to a different OpenSpec change.

If OpenSpec reports state="blocked", resolve the missing required planning artifact through the OpenSpec workflow before continuing implementation. Do not invent missing requirements merely to get past the block.

If OpenSpec reports state="all_done", do not immediately declare success. Perform the final verification below first.

Before claiming completion, independently re-read:

- the current OpenSpec status;
- the current OpenSpec apply instructions;
- all relevant OpenSpec artifacts;
- the repository diff and working-tree state;
- the actual build/test/regression outputs.

Resume from the first genuinely incomplete task. Do not redo completed work unnecessarily.

Implement every remaining required task.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.
- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

At the start of work, after every context compaction, after every resume, and whenever task state is uncertain:

1. Run:
   openspec status --change "fix-surface-visualization-performance" --json

2. Run:
   openspec instructions apply --change "fix-surface-visualization-performance" --json

3. Treat the returned OpenSpec state, instruction, tasks, context, operationGuidance, and contextFiles as authoritative.

4. Read all contextFiles relevant to the remaining work before modifying code.

Resume from the first genuinely incomplete task. Do not redo completed work unnecessarily.

Implement every remaining required task.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.
- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

If the authoritative OpenSpec task set itself changes after attachment, do not silently ignore the difference or invent an independent plan. Reconcile against a fresh OpenSpec apply response before completion.

Run relevant builds, focused tests, integration tests, and regression checks as work progresses. Fix failures caused by this change rather than bypassing them.

Do not weaken, delete, rewrite, reinterpret, or silently defer OpenSpec requirements merely to make implementation easier.

Do not switch to a different OpenSpec change.

If OpenSpec reports state="blocked", resolve the missing required planning artifact through the OpenSpec workflow before continuing implementation. Do not invent missing requirements merely to get past the block.

If OpenSpec reports state="all_done", do not immediately declare success. Perform the final verification below first.

Before claiming completion, independently re-read:

- the current OpenSpec status;
- the current OpenSpec apply instructions;
- all relevant OpenSpec artifacts;
- the repository diff and working-tree state;
- the actual build/test/regression outputs.

Resume from the first genuinely incomplete task. Do not redo completed work unnecessarily.

Implement every remaining required task.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.
- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.
